reason: The abstract evaluates dietary habits in relation to prostatic cancer generally. It reports 100 cases but does not provide sufficient control counts to establish the total analytic sample, and it does not analyze an aggressive endpoint.

estimate_classifications.endpoint_excerpt: Intake of carbohydrates, protein, fat, total calories, fibers, vitamin B and vitamin C were not correlated with the development of prostatic cancer.
estimate_classifications.reason: The vitamin C result concerns development of prostatic cancer generally and provides no aggressive endpoint.

estimate_classifications.endpoint_excerpt: Low daily intake of beta-carotene (RR = 2.13: 95% confidence interval, 1.20-3.77) and of vitamin A (RR = 1.94: 1.10-3.43), as compared to the intake of those substances by BPH controls, were factors significantly correlated with the development of prostatic cancer.
estimate_classifications.reason: The beta-carotene estimate, although stored in reciprocal orientation, pertains to prostatic cancer generally rather than aggressive disease.
